entry.title: kubernetes project #1
entry.summary:
“Run ONE Web App in Kubernetes and Access It”
If someone understands this project, Kubernetes will finally click. You will run one containerized web app in Kubernetes and access it from your browser.
Browser → Service → Pod → Container
What a Pod is Why Kubernetes exists How traffic reaches a container Why Kubernetes networking is different from Docker If this is not clear → nothing else will be clear. ✔ Run an app in Kubernetes Minikube (local Kubernetes) kubectl Docker installed minikube start
Verify: kubectl get nodes
Expected: NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION minikube Ready control-plane ...
Why: Kubernetes always runs workloads on nodes. Create file: pod.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: hello-pod labels: app: hello spec: containers: - name: hello-container image: nginx ports: - containerPort: 80
Apply it: kubectl apply -f pod.yaml
Check: kubectl get pods
Why: A Pod is the smallest thing Kubernetes runs — not a container. kubectl describe pod hello-pod
Key things to notice: Pod IP Container status Events Explain to students: Kubernetes assigned an IP, started the container, and is monitoring it. Create file: service.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: name: hello-service spec: type: NodePort selector: app: hello ports: - port: 80 targetPort: 80 nodePort: 30007
Apply: kubectl apply -f service.yaml
Check: kubectl get svc
Why: Pod IPs are not stable. stable access. Run: minikube ip
Open browser: http://<MINIKUBE_IP>:30007
You should see: Welcome to nginx!
This is Kubernetes working. Delete the Pod: kubectl delete pod hello-pod
Check: kubectl get pods
Result: Explain: This is why Pods alone are NOT production-ready.
Concept You now understand
Pod Smallest unit
Service Stable networking
NodePort External access
Labels How Services find Pods
Why Deployments exist Pods die
Kubernetes did not recreate the Pod Deployments next

entry.title: Coding Challenge Practice - Question 94
📱 WebSockets Explained Like You're 5
entry.summary:
A phone call instead of texting Day 10 of 149 👉 Full deep-dive with code examples Texting (HTTP): You send a message You wait for reply Conversation over To talk again? Send another message and wait Phone Call (WebSocket): You connect once Talk anytime, both ways Instant responses Stay connected until you hang up Regular web pages use HTTP: Browser: "Any new messages?" Server: "Nope" (1 second later) Browser: "Any new messages?" Server: "Nope" (1 second later) Browser: "Any new messages?" Server: "Yes! Here's one!"
This is like texting someone "ANY NEWS?!" every second. Annoying and wasteful! Browser: "Let's open a phone line" Server: "Connected! ✅"
(Server gets a new message) Server: "Hey! New message for you!" (instantly pushes)
(Browser sends a message) Browser: "Sending this!" (instantly sent)
Both can talk anytime. No waiting. No constant asking. 💬 Chat apps (WhatsApp, Discord) 📈 Stock tickers (live price updates) 🎮 Multiplayer games (real-time action) 🔔 Notifications (instant alerts) 📝 Google Docs (see others typing live) WebSockets keep a live connection open so browser and server can talk instantly, anytime, without waiting. 🔗 Enjoying these? Follow for daily ELI5 explanations! Making complex tech concepts simple, one day at a time.
